title: Forbearance of claims and settlement
summary: Giving up or delaying a legal claim can be consideration for a settlement promise, subject to limits concerning the claim and the claimant’s belief in it.
notes:
Dyer addresses a claim assumed to be legally invalid. The Iowa court held that invalidity alone did not defeat consideration when the claimant honestly believed the claim could be valid, and it remanded for examination of good faith. The casebook also records jurisdictions using more demanding formulations. Identify what claim was surrendered, what was promised for that surrender, and what the claimant believed at the time. A knowingly baseless threat made for harassment presents a different problem from an honest dispute.

Dyer uses Restatement § 74 to distinguish doubt about a claim from honest belief in a claim that proves invalid. The policy of encouraging settlements does not protect knowingly baseless demands. Fiege supplies a paternity-claim comparison, while the notes ask how litigation certification duties and other legal limits bear on promises not to sue. Settlement of uncertainty is itself a bargained-for benefit, but a court must still determine what was promised and surrendered.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 62–68. Open assigned page 62.
